verdict.rationale: Sumsub's Liveness check documentation names specific spoofing vectors it defends against: deepfakes, AI-generated images, paper masks, photos of a screen and dolls. Analysts can also review Liveness results in the applicant profile. The evidence never mentions camera-injection or virtual-camera attack detection, and the deepfake defense is a single summary sentence rather than a documented detection method. Missing for 10: documented camera/video-injection attack detection, in-depth technical documentation of the deepfake and AI-face detection methods, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a risk analyst, the vendor documents specific defenses against AI-generated faces, deepfakes, and camera-injection attacks — named detection capabilities, not just a marketing mention of fraud

citations.quote: In under a second, it confirms the applicant is a real, live person (not a deepfake, AI-generated image, paper mask, photo of a screen, or doll)
In the profile, navigate to the Liveness section and review the results.
